text:
Can your business benefit from SEO?

Quick test. Would a customer type what you do plus your suburb into Google?

"mobile mechanic Penrith"
"dentist Glenelg"
"bookkeeper Toowoomba"

If yes, they're already searching. They'll find you or the business down the road.

Local SEO is a lot like the gym.

Nobody gets fit from one big session.

You turn up week after week, long after it gets boring.

That's how I got my own business ranking. Profile kept current. Helpful pages. Plenty of patience.

Boring works.

How often does Google change how it ranks websites?

Big core updates land several times a year. Smaller tweaks roll out in between.

You don't need to follow any of it.

Stay on the tools. Leave the Google watching to someone who does it every day.

Who SEO suits, plainly:

You serve a local area.
People search for what you do.
You can give it a few months to build.

Who it doesn't suit:

You need the phone ringing by Friday.

That's a job for Google Ads first. Then build SEO underneath it.

A dentist in Kingston asks why she'd pay someone for SEO when it's all on YouTube.

Fair question.

She could also do her own tax return.

Google changes the rules a few times a year, and small stuff in between.

Someone should be keeping up so she can keep seeing patients.

Someone walks into your shop and says "I'd like to book in."

You hand them a scrap of paper. "Leave your number, we'll call you sometime."

That's how most Facebook lead forms have worked for years.

Meta now lets people pick a time straight after the form. I'd switch it on.
